subject: Re: Proposal — phased capped NetTerm sprint & billing entity routing
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aegishealth.com>, Procurement - Aegis Health <procurement@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: phased capped NetTerm sprint & billing entity routing

Hi Liam / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time on Tuesday — great alignment on scope. Per our conversation, attached is a concise proposal for a phased payment schedule that lets Aegis ramp usage without exceeding internal credit thresholds while giving Redwood predictable cash flow during the initial ramp. High level: 

- Request: Standard Net45 for recurring invoices, with a temporary outstanding credit cap of $250,000 for the first 90 days.
- If Aegis prefers longer terms initially, we can provide a Net60 option but with a phased holdback/escrow on taxes and a modest early-payment discount to align incentives.
- Billing entity routing: we need to confirm which Aegis legal entity will accept invoices for this engagement (US HQ vs EU subsidiary). Correct routing prevents VAT/tax mismatches.

Requested next steps:
1) Review the attached proposed schedule (Redwood_proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx) and confirm preferred term (Net45 vs Net60).
2) Provide the billing entity name + AP contact and, if applicable, the VAT/tax registration certificate for the paying entity.
3) If procurement needs PO/contract redlines, send the doc and we will coordinate legal.

I put Marissa on copy — she will confirm the temporary credit cap and finance checks once you confirm entity.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aegishealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement - Aegis Health <procurement@aegishealth.com>, Accounts Payable - Aegis Health <ap@aegishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 10:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased capped NetTerm sprint & billing entity routing

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear proposal and the schedule. A couple of clarifications from our side before we sign: 

1) Term preference: Our centralized AP org typically pushes for Net60 for new vendors during pilot windows, but we are open to Net45 given appropriate credit guardrails.

2) Billing entity: For contract purposes the payer will be Aegis Health, Inc. (US). We also have an EU subsidiary (Aegis Health Europe Ltd) that has VAT registration for EMEA consumption; when EU teams consume services they need EU invoices to avoid cross-border VAT complications.

3) Tax/VAT evidence: We'll be able to provide a VAT registration certificate for the EU entity, but that will take 2–3 business days.

4) SOW redlines: Attached is a lightly redlined SOW that tries to consolidate milestones and the acceptance criteria. If Redwood can accept the payment waterfall where milestone invoices trigger acceptance and a 10% retainage is held for 30 days, we can proceed to issue a PO.

Regarding terms: would Redwood consider Net60 for the first 90 days and then moving to Net45 after historic payment runs? Alternatively, an early-pay discount (1–2%) for payment within 15 days would make Net45 more palatable.

Attaching: Aegis_SOW_redline_v1.docx

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Director, Procurement — Aegis Health
Attachment: Aegis_SOW_redline_v1.docx (redline doc)

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased capped NetTerm sprint & billing entity routing

Liam — appreciate the redlines and the context. A few operational items from finance: 

- Credit cap: We can provision a temporary outstanding credit cap of $250,000 for the initial 90-day pilot. That cap is conditional on: (a) PO issuance with agreed billing entity, and (b) receipt of vendor KYC (W-9 for US entity, VAT certificate for EU entity when EU invoicing applies).
- Retainage: Redwood can accept the 10% retainage per milestone for 30 days, but retainage will be deducted from available credit until released. Please note this impacts the effective spend against the credit cap.
- Net terms: We are prepared to accept Net60 for the first 60 days as a courtesy, if Aegis provides a PO and commits to a Net45 from month 3 onward. Alternatively, Net45 from day one with a 1% early-payment discount for payments within 15 days is also on the table.
- Tax routing: Please confirm the exact legal name and remit-to address for whichever entity will be billed — billing to the wrong legal entity creates tax headaches we want to avoid.

I have attached a simple invoice schedule Excel that maps invoice dates, milestones, and retainage. Once we have the PO and entity certificate, finance will lift the temporary cap quickly.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx (invoice schedule)

Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased capped NetTerm sprint & billing entity routing

Hi all — quick commercial suggestion from my side to close this without introducing operational friction: 

Option A (preferred for cash predictability): Net45 standard. As a concession, Redwood will offer a 1.0% early-payment discount for invoices paid within 15 calendar days. Temporary credit cap $250k for 90 days.

Option B (if Aegis needs more runway): Net60 for the first 90 days with a 0.5% administrative surcharge on invoices issued during that window. After 90 days, terms revert to Net45. This removes the need for an escrow but slightly increases cost during the extended window.

Operational asks: PO number, exact remit entity for invoicing, and either (a) W-9 + bank contact (US), or (b) VAT certificate + EU remit address if invoices go to the EU entity.

If procurement confirms Option A we can generate the first invoice after milestone 1 and apply the early-pay discount programmatically to any payment that hits within 15 days. Happy to take this over a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
AP & Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aegishealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounts Payable - Aegis Health <ap@aegishealth.com>, Procurement - Aegis Health <procurement@aegishealth.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased capped NetTerm sprint & billing entity routing

Hi Priya / Marissa / Marcus — thanks for the flexibility. We will accept Option A: Net45 with a 1.0% early-payment discount for payments made within 15 days. Confirming the payer and remit: Aegis Health, Inc. (US) — remit to the US entity for this engagement. AP will issue PO #AEG-PO-49821 by COB Monday.

We are attaching the signed SOW and the VAT certificate for our EU subsidiary for completeness (the EU certificate is for future cross-border consumption; not applicable to US invoices).

Attachments: Aegis_Master_SOW_v3_signed.pdf, Aegis_tax_entity_certificate.pdf

Next steps for Redwood: please send an invoice schedule and the final invoice remit-to details so our AP team can validate the PO match. We'll route payment per Net45 schedule; we will flag any early payments to claim the discount.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Director, Procurement — Aegis Health
Attachment: Aegis_Master_SOW_v3_signed.pdf (signed SOW)
Attachment: Aegis_tax_entity_certificate.pdf (VAT registration for EU subsidiary)
